objective: Spot the wrong statements about kite line and say what it should be.

narration.text: Before each flight, wind the kite line neatly onto a reel.
Braided line stretches less than twisted line under the same load.
Thicker line always lets a kite fly higher because it is stronger.
Gloves protect your hands when a strong gust pulls on the line.
A line rated for twice the kite's pull never wears out.
After landing, wind the line back evenly so it does not tangle.

planted.misconception: Thicker line makes a kite fly higher.
planted.whyWrong: Thicker line is heavier and catches more wind, so its weight and drag pull the kite lower.
acceptableCorrections: A thinner, lighter line lets a kite climb higher because it adds less weight and drag.
planted.exceptions: In a very strong wind a heavier line may be needed so it does not snap.

planted.misconception: A strongly rated line lasts for ever.
planted.whyWrong: Sunlight and rubbing weaken a line over time, so its real strength drops below the rating.
acceptableCorrections: Even a highly rated line must be checked for frays before each flight because wear lowers its strength.
replace the cord when it looks worn

explain: strength drops below the rating|loses strength
correct: rating does not last|strength is not permanent
